read.sections.0.text.note: Language names take their usual Thai forms: กวารานี (Guaraní), โซมาลี, ทมิฬ, มลายู, ปารากวัย. The checker warns that "Guaraní" no longer appears in Latin letters; it is a real language name, so it is written in Thai like the others. The lesson keeps "English" as the language learners may be judged on, exactly as the English does; a reviewer may ask whether a Thai-language version should say so differently (not changed here).
read.sections.0.text.source: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and care. Hearing a word you know can help you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual. In Paraguay, for example, many people speak both Spanish and Guaraní. Someone who speaks Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. How well a person speaks English does not show how clever they are. It does not show whether their ideas matter.
read.sections.0.text.back: People use language to share news, tell jokes, share memories and show care. Hearing words you know helps you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world speak several languages. For example, in Paraguay many people speak both Spanish and Guarani. People who speak Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. How well a person speaks English doesn't tell how clever they are, and doesn't tell whether their ideas matter.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: People use language to share news, jokes and care. A word you know can help you feel welcome. Many people are multilingual. They speak two or more languages. In Paraguay, lots of people speak Spanish and Guaraní. If you speak two or three languages, you can help others. That is a real skill. Good English does not show how smart you are. All people's ideas matter.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: People use language to share news, tell jokes and show care. Words you know help you feel welcome. Many people speak several languages. They speak two languages or more. In Paraguay many people speak Spanish and Guarani. If you can speak two or three languages, you can help others. That is a real skill. Speaking English well doesn't show how clever you are. Everyone's ideas matter.

read.sections.1.text.note: Deaf communities = ชุมชนคนหูหนวก (Thai has no capital-D distinction). pictogram = ภาพสัญลักษณ์. accessible = เข้าถึงได้ (KEY_TERMS).
read.sections.1.text.source: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign languages, which are full languages with their own grammar. The United Nations says there are more than 300 sign languages in the world. People also use gestures, pictures and clear design. The pictogram on the notice shows food, a clock, a calendar and a map. This makes the notice more accessible, because more people can understand the main message. But a picture cannot give every detail, such as what to bring. A volunteer who can interpret still helps.
read.sections.1.text.back: Communication isn't only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign languages, which are complete languages with their own grammar. The United Nations says the world has more than 300 sign languages. People also use gestures, pictures and clear design. The pictograms on the notice show food, a clock, a calendar and a map. This makes the notice more accessible, because more people can understand the main message. But pictures can't give every detail, such as what to bring. So a volunteer who can interpret still helps.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Communication is more than talking and writing. Deaf people use sign languages. These are full languages. There are more than 300 of them. People also use hands, faces and pictures. The notice has pictures of food, a clock and a map. This makes it more accessible. More people can understand it. But a picture cannot say what to bring. A helper who can interpret is still useful.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Communication is more than speaking and writing. Deaf people use sign language. Sign language is a complete language. The world has more than 300 sign languages. People also use hands, faces and pictures. The notice has pictures of food, a clock and a map. This makes the notice more accessible. More people can understand. But pictures can't say what to bring. So a helper who can interpret is still useful.

read.sections.2.text.note: "coffee", qahwah, kahveh and caffè stay in Latin letters: they are the words being traced. The Thai word กาแฟ is not added because the English does not mention it.
read.sections.2.text.source: Languages change over time. They also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word “coffee” travelled a long way. It started as the Arabic word qahwah. It became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, and then it reached English. Many languages are also related. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one language family, because they grew from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another. Each one carries the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.
read.sections.2.text.back: Languages change over time. Languages also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word "coffee" travelled a long way. It started from the Arabic word qahwah, then became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, and then reached English. Many languages are also relatives. English, Hindi and Persian are in the same language family because they grew from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa are in another language family. No language is better than another. Each language holds the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: Languages change over time. They take words from each other. Look at the word “coffee”. It began in Arabic. Then it went into Turkish and Italian. Then it came into English. Some languages are like cousins. They grew from one old language. So they are in one language family. English, Hindi and Persian are in one. Arabic, Somali and Hausa are in a different one. No language is the best. Each one holds the stories of the people who speak it.

write.example.source: I would add the notice in two or three languages that visitors use. This helps because more people can read it in a language they know. I would also add a helper at the door who can interpret. This helps people ask questions, like what to bring. One limit is that a written notice cannot help people who do not read. The pictures and the helper can help with that. This shows that using more than one way to share a message helps more people feel welcome.

Also, I would have a helper at the door who can interpret. This lets people ask questions, such as what to bring. One limit is that people who can't read won't benefit from a written notice. Pictures and helpers can help with this. This shows that using several ways to get a message across helps more people feel welcome.

watch.summary.source: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke one language moved apart. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed the way it spoke. New words came in, and sounds changed. In time, one language became several languages. Languages that grew from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, like numbers, to find these links. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so experts check them with care. It can be hard to say where one language ends and another begins. So different experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with an idea: a language that sounds new to you may be related to one you know.
watch.summary.back: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke the same language spread apart. They went to live in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years each group changed the way it spoke. New words came in and sounds changed. In the end, one language became many languages. Languages that grew from the same old language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, such as numbers, to find these connections. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so experts must check these words carefully. It can be hard to say where one language ends and another begins, so different experts count different numbers of languages in the world, from 3,000 to 8,000. The video ends with the idea that a language that sounds new to you may be related to a language you know.

watch.keyPoints.1.source: Related languages grew from one older language.
watch.keyPoints.1.back: Related languages grew from the same old language.

watch.keyPoints.2.source: Languages also borrow words from their neighbours.
watch.keyPoints.2.back: Languages also borrow words from neighbours.

watch.contentNote.source: The video opens with the Tower of Babel story as a hook, then describes early human groups moving apart. The narration is fast and the vocabulary is quite advanced, so pause often or use the written summary.
watch.contentNote.back: The video opens with the story of the Tower of Babel to catch interest, then tells about early human groups spreading apart. The narrator speaks fast and uses fairly hard vocabulary, so it's best to pause the video often or use the written summary.
